pride_data.title: Proteomic profiling of a biological sample (human serum) derived from the surface of the AFM chip
pride_data.projectDescription: Mass spectrometric analysis was used to identify proteins from a biological plasma samples covalently immobilized on the surface of an AFM chip using cross-linkers.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: To carry out trypsinolysis, add a solution containing 10 µl of trypsin at a concentration of 0.1 g/l, 50 µl of TEAB (50 mM) and 1000 µl of deionized water to tubes with AFM chips so that the solution completely covers the mica. F Then place the tubes with AFM chips in a shaker-incubator (18 hours, 37 °C, 140 rpm. Then put the tubes in a shaker for 60 minutes (800 rpm, 40 °C) for mixing. After that, mix the tubes on the Vortex MIX 1 minute and 10 minutes in a centrifuge (9000 rpm). Remove the ACM chip from the tube with the tryptic mixture with tweezers and wash it with acetonitrile on each side using a laboratory dispenser of 40 µl. Wash out into a test tube with trypsin lysate, then apply 40 µl of acetonitrile to the inside of the lid and close the tube. Unscrew tubes with tryptic mixture in a centrifuge for 10 minutes, 9000 rpm and use further for panoramic analysis. Panoramic mass spectrometry is performed on a Q ExactiveTM HF Hybrid Quadrupole- OrbitrapTM instrument, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Rockwell, IL, USA), which allows panoramic protein searches and is used in routine analysis. The peptides for each sample are separated by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC, Ultimate 3000 Nano LC System, Thermo Scientific, Rockwell, IL, USA) on a 15 cm long, 75 µm id C18 column (Acclaim® PepMap™ RSLC, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Rockwell, IL, USA). Elute the peptides with a gradient of 5–35% buffer B (80% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid) over 115 min at a flow rate of 0.3 µl–1 min. Total run time including 90 min to reach 99% buffer B, 10 min wash with 99% buffer B and 15 min re-equilibrate with buffer A (0.1% formic acid).
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: For each sample, the resulting raw Q ExactiveTM mass spectrometer RAW files were analyzed with the MaxQuant software (version 1.5.5.1, Jurgen Cox, Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry, Martinsried, Germany) with built-in Andromeda search engine. Bioinformatics analysis is carried out using the Perseus program, version 2.0.6.0 (Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry, Germany). For each sample, the mass spectrometric analysis data is compared based on the area under the peak of the parent ion with the calculation of the LFQ value using the built-in algorithm.
keywords: Mica; atomic force microscopy (afm); cross linker; protein immobilization; lc-ms
